chunks: One of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadrami, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'My family eats the meat of the goat and does not eat the meat of the lamb.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' I said: 'They say that it is meat which stirs the bitterness (acidity).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, known of anything better than the lamb, He would have sacrificed with it,' meaning Isaac. This is how it has come in the hadith.

key_terms.لَفَدَى بِهِ: He would have sacrificed with it

ai.seo_question: Why do some families avoid eating lamb meat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) refutes the pre-Islamic Arab custom of avoiding lamb meat due to its perceived ability to increase bitterness or acidity in the body. He cites the precedent of Prophet Isaac (peace be upon him), implying that if lamb were inferior or harmful, Allah would have chosen a better sacrifice for him. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly view that cultural superstitions should not override divine preference, as evidenced by the Quranic narrative of the ram's substitution.

en.hubeali: One of our companions, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Hazramy, from sa’ad Bin Sa’ad who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> that, ‘My family are eating the meat of the goat, and are not eating the meat of the lamb’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why?’ I said, ‘They are saying that it is a meat which stirs the bitterness (acidity)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Had Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Known of (anything) better than the lamb, He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Sacrificed by it, meaning Is’haq’. (He, the narrator said), ‘This is how it has come in the Hadeeth’.
en.sarwar: 3. Certain persons of our people have narrated from Ja‘far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadramiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘My family eats the meat of goats but not that of sheep.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Why they do so?’ I replied, ‘They say that it excites bitterness (stomach acid).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Had Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, known anything better than sheep He would have presented it as ransom for Ishaq.’” This is how it has come in Hadith.
